mainKeyword: cordless lawn edgers with batteries and chargers
guideTitle: Best Cordless Lawn Edgers With Batteries and Chargers (2026)
metaDescription: Six cordless lawn edgers that ship with a battery and charger, compared on pack size, voltage, number of packs and what each bundle really gives you.
expertTake: The Greenworks 40V 8 Inch kit is the pick for most buyers because the battery, charger and brushless edger are matched and the pack is a platform worth owning. The goodjob 20V is the value pick for two packs and a fast charger. Skip the bundles if you already own a compatible pack, since a bare tool costs less and you avoid duplicating a charger.
introParagraphs: A cordless tool is only as useful as the battery in the box. Two edgers with the same motor and blade can feel completely different if one ships with a big pack and a fast charger and the other with a small pack and a slow one.

Reading a bundle well means looking beyond the word included. How much energy does the pack hold, how long does the charger take, is there a second pack, and will the battery fit other tools you might buy later? This guide answers those questions for six kits.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 8 Inch Brushless Edger Kit, 4.0Ah battery
products.description:
This kit sets the standard for a matched bundle. A 40V 4.0Ah pack and a charger arrive with a brushless 8 inch edger, so every part is designed to work together and the motor is efficient enough to make the most of the pack. A curb wheel and tool free depth adjustment complete a well rounded tool.

The 40V pack is also a platform battery, which means it fits other Greenworks 40V tools you might add later, such as a trimmer or blower, and that you can share one charger across all of them. That is the long term value of a name brand kit, and it is the reason this bundle ranks above cheaper ones with sealed packs that fit nothing else. Against the 2 x 2.0Ah bundles, it has the same total capacity in one pack, but a single pack means a pause to recharge.

Charge the pack after each use, store it indoors and do not leave it on the charger for weeks. A partly charged pack in a cool place keeps its capacity longest. Because the tool and pack are designed as a pair, the motor controller can be tuned to the pack, which is why a name brand kit often runs a little cooler and a little longer than a mix and match setup. Check that the charger lights are easy to read before you commit.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a matched kit on a platform they can extend.
pros: Matched brushless tool, pack and charger
Curb wheel and tool free depth
Efficient motor makes the most of the pack
cons: Single pack means a charging pause
Higher price tier than the 20V kits

products.name: DEWALT 60V MAX Cordless Lawn Edger Kit, FLEXVOLT battery and charger
products.description:
This is the heavyweight in the lineup. A 60V MAX FLEXVOLT battery and charger come with the tool, a 7.5 inch hardened steel blade cuts up to 2.5 inches deep, and a large guide wheel helps the tool move along the edge. The listing also notes universal attachment capability, so the same power head can accept other attachments.

A 60V pack stores far more energy than a 20V pack, which means a deep, tough edging job drains it slower. The FLEXVOLT line is also built to be shared with other DeWalt tools that take this pack, making the bundle a good entry to the platform. The cost is the highest price tier among the six, and the 60V pack is heavy.

Store the pack indoors, charge it before the season starts and keep the contacts clean. Because the platform is high power, it suits yards with real edging demands rather than light touch ups. The cutting depth of up to 2.5 inches means one pass can restore a lost border that a 1.5 inch tool would need several passes to recover, which saves battery in the long run. Expect to carry more weight, and plan your route so you can set the tool down at the ends.
products.bestFor: Heavy edging jobs and buyers building a 60V tool collection.

products.name: goodjob 20V Cordless Lawn Edger, 9 inch blade, 2 batteries
products.description:
Two 2.0Ah packs and a fast charger turn one battery's worth of runtime into two with a swap. That is the main argument for this bundle: you keep working while the first pack charges. A 400W motor drives a 9 inch steel blade with three depth settings and dual guide wheels.

The packs are small, which means each one drains quickly in dense soil, but having two is a practical answer for medium borders. The fast charger shortens the wait, and is a better arrangement than one slow charger and one big pack for people who work in short bursts.

It is a lesser known brand, so a battery that fails later may be hard to replace. Number the packs and alternate them so that wear is even. If one pack ever seems to run down much faster than the other, retire it to light duty and consider a replacement, since a single weak cell in a bundle is the most common reason a kit feels tired after a couple of seasons. Keep the fast charger on a shelf away from damp.
products.bestFor: Medium borders where a quick swap is worth more than a big single pack.
cons: Replacement packs may be hard to find

products.name: EWORK 20V Cordless Lawn Edger, 2 batteries, charger, indicator
products.description:
A battery indicator on the pack tells you how much charge is left before you start a long border, which is a feature many bundles skip. Two 2.0Ah batteries and a charger are included, and a 500W motor with built in protection drives a 9 inch metal blade at 3500 rpm.

Four depth settings give more steps than the three on several rivals. It is a brushed motor, so efficiency is lower than the Greenworks, but it is a sensible design for small lawns. Against the goodjob it adds an indicator and a more powerful motor rating.

Check the indicator before each outing, rotate the packs and clean the charging contacts with a dry cloth. A battery gauge is more useful than it sounds on a tool like this, because you can decide at the start whether to edge the long side of the lot now or wait for a recharge, and it stops a mid job surprise. The built in protection also helps a pack survive a stall in a root.
products.bestFor: Users who want to know their charge level before they start.

products.name: ECOWORK 20V Cordless Lawn Edger and Trencher, 4.0Ah battery
products.description:
A single 4.0Ah pack gives the same stored energy as the two 2.0Ah packs on the goodjob, with one battery to track and charge. A charger comes in the box, and the tool offers four cutting heights and a three position parallel guide on a 9 inch blade.

The tradeoff against the two pack bundles is the pause: when the pack is empty the job stops until it recharges. For a short or medium border one pack is enough, and the simplicity is a plus. Against the Greenworks kit it is a lower cost 20V option without a brushless motor.

Remove the pack after each use and store it partly charged. Keep the contacts clean for a good connection. If you expect to edge more than one side of a corner lot, think about a second pack of the same platform, which on the 20V line is a simple add on and doubles the time you can work between charges.
products.bestFor: Short to medium borders where one pack is enough.
pros: Four heights and a parallel guide
cons: Single pack means a charging pause

products.name: Jenixy 20V Cordless Lawn Edger, 9 inch brushless motor, battery

specList.label: Battery
specList.value: Included, capacity not stated in the title

products.description:
A brushless motor and an included battery at a low tier make this the economy kit. The motor reaches 3200 rpm and drives a 9 inch blade with three depth levels, and the listing says it ships with a battery.

The weak spot is documentation: the title does not state the pack capacity or charger detail, so check the full listing before you buy. A brushless motor helps a small pack go further, which is part of the value here. Against the goodjob it has a brushless motor, but fewer stated details on the pack.

Treat the battery as a wear item. Charge it after use, avoid deep drains and store it in a cool place. Open the full listing and the manual before you start to confirm the pack capacity and charge time, and keep a note of them with the receipt, so any later replacement pack can be matched correctly.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Amp hours measure the battery's fuel tank. A 4.0Ah pack, like the Greenworks 40V and ECOWORK, holds twice the energy of a 2.0Ah pack at the same voltage. The goodjob and EWORK ship two 2.0Ah packs, which equals one 4.0Ah pack in total energy but allows a swap, and a swap is worth more than it sounds: the first pack cools while the second works, and a cooler pack lives longer.

Voltage sets how much power the motor can draw, and the platform decides what else the pack can run. The DEWALT 60V MAX FLEXVOLT is a high power platform, the Greenworks 40V suits mid power, and the 20V kits are lighter duty. Pick a platform you will extend, since a spare pack costs about half the tool. If you intend to buy a mower or a blower next, choose the platform for those tools first and the edger second, because the largest savings come from sharing the pack across the whole set.

A fast charger, as in the goodjob bundle, shortens the wait and makes a two pack swap practical. A slow charger can take hours, and a single pack kit with a slow charger means the job ends for the day. Check the charge time in the full listing, and compare it with how long a typical border takes you, since a charger that returns a pack in an hour fits a two pack workflow, while one that takes four hours does not.

buyingCriteria.criterion: One big pack versus two small
buyingCriteria.explanation: One 4.0Ah pack is simple but forces a charging break. Two 2.0Ah packs let you swap and keep going, but each runs out faster on a hard cut. For a long edge, two packs win, and for a short one a single pack is enough.

An indicator, as on the EWORK, lets you plan. Built in protection against overload and deep discharge extends pack life. Without either, you find out the pack is empty when the blade slows, which in the middle of a long curb wastes time and can leave a ragged end to the cut. Look for a pack that cuts out cleanly and protects its own cells.

Packs wear out after a few years of use. A name brand platform like Greenworks or DEWALT offers replacements for years, while a lesser known brand may not. If you plan to keep the tool a long time, favor the platform with a future. Ask yourself whether you would still be able to buy the exact pack in three years, because the pack is the part of any cordless tool that is most likely to be replaced before the tool itself wears out.

faq.q: Is a kit with a battery better than a bare tool?
faq.a: A kit is better if you have no compatible pack, since you can use it at once. A bare tool saves money if you already own a pack.

faq.q: How long does a battery edger run?
faq.a: It depends on pack size, soil and depth. A short border may use a fraction of a pack, and a neglected one may need two.

faq.q: Should I buy a spare battery?
faq.a: If your borders are long, yes. A spare doubles the working day.

faq.q: Can I use these batteries in other tools?
faq.a: Only within the same platform. The Greenworks 40V and DEWALT 60V packs fit their own tool families.

faq.q: How long does a pack last in years?
faq.a: Several years with sensible charging, but capacity fades over time. Avoid heat and deep discharge.
